## 2026-10-10 000 DECISION: parallel source tasks write per-source staging files, consolidated once by task 211

235" is exactly the PENDING subset of the parsed tokens (203a, 203b, 211, 212b, 301,
306e, 307d are all done and dropped from the note; only 212 and 235 are pending) - the
note reproduces the tokenizer, confirming the theory. 239's wait on 212 is legitimate
(cover.py is 212's in-flight file; not a code dependency, a same-file gate) and
parked behind 212.

Fix (box 5 of 000 is exactly "the numbers of the tasks that must be finished first, or
none" - a format-line cleanup on agent-created files, precedent 302a/308/309 from

# Task 001 fit-gate

## 2026-10-10 001 DECISION: the gate judges by metric conjunction, not by one score
Recon spikes (no code in the repo yet; scripts in /tmp, results in the task hand-over): (1) ALL-ink 4-neighbour
ridge contrast on the DEM fails (castle-rising true fit scored worst, -0.653 vs null -0.07); (2) autowalls-extracted
wall template + fit_plate's stroke-normal contrast separates true from 60 m/10°/15% on castle-rising but NOT on
bergues (flat town, ploughed walls: true -0.205 worst), and its one-sidedness lets any template score +0.53 on
hilly cross-site ground; (3) old-map ink proximity is saturated on dense maps. So the gate will combine: pair-
consistency residuals, old-map correlation (spike 4, pending), DEM-vs-search-matched-null where relief is strong.
Chosen over a single relief score because docs/autofit.md finding 2 already proved the relief score has false
peaks; the 4th wrong-fit type (best placement on another site's ground) is constructed to beat any single-score
gate, so evidence must be independent per layer.

## 2026-10-10 001 DECISION: held-out selection and test strategy
Held-out = 8 of the 21 fits by numpy.random.default_rng(20260101).choice over sorted filenames (to be written in
docs/gate.md before the run); the other 13 are the dev set for threshold selection only. Test re-run strategy:
commit per-fit input caches as data/gate/*.npz (DEM, map ink, plate ink, wall template, pairs) so the test is
offline and deterministic; the gate program itself fetches DEMs at runtime when its cache is absent. .npy is
gitignored globally but .npz is not (only data/autofit/*.npz is).

## 2026-10-10 001 BLOCKER: none yet - design iteration, not a repeated failure

## 2026-10-10 001 DECISION: pair-consistency residuals alone cannot be the gate - dev true fits are sloppy
Solved-transform per-pair residuals on the 12 DEV fits (held-out untouched): medians 3.7-53.1 m, maxes

are the 60 m / cross-site layer of the conjunction; rotation/scale need the image conjunct (spike 6 dir_frac
is the candidate, run in progress).

## 2026-10-10 001 DECISION: all six image-structure metrics fail (spikes 1-6) - the gate pivots to pure geometry
Spike 4 (blurred plate-ink vs blurred map-ink Pearson): castle-rising true +0.386 < null_max +0.424; bergues true
+0.052 < null +0.484; maiden-castle true -0.048 < null +0.411 (mirrored +0.379); serpent-mound true -0.111 <
null +0.645. Cross-site searches scored +0.653 and +0.972 - dense maps correlate with anything. FAIL.
Spike 5 (autowalls wall points within 10 m of density-filtered map strokes): no separation at any site
(castle-rising true 0.718 vs moved 0.720 / x0.85 0.841; bergues off-grid; mirrored is the only case killed). FAIL.
Spike 6 (same but requiring the wall normal to align with the stroke across-direction, |cos| >= 0.7, 15 m
window): castle-rising true 0.420 vs x0.85 0.450 (wrong HIGHER); bergues true 0.056 (only 23% of its wall points
in-box) with all cases 0.03-0.06; maiden-castle true 0.259 vs x0.85 0.331; serpent-mound true 0.252 vs x1.15
0.338. Cross-site: castle plate on bergues map 0.457 (> bergues's own true). corr_ws returned n/a everywhere.
FAIL. Combined with spikes 1-3 (DEM ridge, DEM wall contrast, ink proximity - see archive), no image statistic
separates 60 m / 10 deg / 15% / cross-site on dense old maps, because those shifts (<= 0.1745 r, 0.15 r, 60 m)
are smaller than the map's structural wavelength. The gate will therefore be geometric: pair-residual magnitude
catches 60 m move (median exactly 60 m vs dev max 53.1 m) and cross-site (km-scale), and a residual-vs-radius
pattern (10 deg / x1.15 add 0.1745 r / 0.15 r per point, a radial gradient a true sloppy fit does not have)
must catch rotation/scale. Spike 7 (next session): measure those statistics on the 12 dev docs and the four
wrong types to set thresholds. The gate stays image-free -> no skimage, no requirements.txt change needed.

## 2026-10-10 200 DECISION: set_field dropped the line terminator - record would have glued jsonl rows; fixed before the first real run
Where: fit/evidence.py (set_field, rewrite, record); tests/test_evidence.py (new test_record_appends_evidence_without_touching_existing_bytes)
json.dumps never emits a trailing newline and record's rewrite() replaces whole lines via writelines, so every
recorded line would have been concatenated with the next (corrupt jsonl). The bug was latent since iteration 10
(the sample file predates the final set_field; record had never run on a real file). Caught this session by
running the real set_field on a real line before the record run. Fix: set_field appends "\n" iff the input line
ended with one. The new test runs the record CLI on a tmp fixture (a hand-tied, an unrecorded and a sentinel
commons row, two book rows) and asserts: line count and terminators intact, untouched rows byte-identical,
recorded rows keep every original byte as a prefix, "evidence" is the only and last key added. The test first
failed after its own source rows got recorded (it compared against the raw line, which then contained the
evidence key the fixture strips) - fixed to compare against the stripped fixture line; that comparison is what
pins "extend rows, never move or delete them".

check over the recorded book rows FAILed 52 of the 135 legitimate matches, two families: (a) "stored place
state='ohio|wisconsin' recomputes to None" - match_row injects the book-scope default state (BOOK_SCOPE) into
the place when the printed text names none; my check recomputed from printed text only. (b) "the row does not
name 'X'" - the matcher ties rows by distinctive-token sharing and exact phrase/alias lookup (a title printing
"Pulpit Hill" ties "Small multivallate hillfort on Pulpit Hill" via an alias; "The Square at Newark" ties
"Newark Earthworks"); my check required the site's full name as a substring of the printed text - stricter than
the rule the match was made under. Both are the same failure mode as iteration 11's name_keys bug: check
re-stating the matcher's rules instead of using them. Fix per the module's own contract ("the check must use
the matcher's own rules"): extracted the row-side extraction (row_inputs: toks, name_toks, place incl. the
book-scope default, phrases, regions) and the per-candidate rule (score_candidate: region/state/county
contradictions -> reject, county bonus, token share, exact bump, the three why clauses) from match_row into
functions both sides share. check_book_caption now: recomputes the row side from the printed text (must equal
the stored place dict exactly), checks the site snapshot (id/qid/name/lon/lat), the HAND table, then the
matcher's one-pair evaluation (is_exact via the site's current lookup keys vs the row's phrase keys) must
reproduce the stored score (round(…,2) equality) with an empty why and both thresholds. The runner-up margin
stays stored (the catalog is not monotone - a new site can take the margin; a full re-run would fail on data
growth, decided iteration 10). No record-format change was needed: tokens and place are recomputable from the
printed text, so the existing "evidence/1" records work as is. The refactor was proven behavior-neutral with a
one-off before/after run (matches.jsonl hash 30f099b1… and the stdout summary byte-identical; matches.jsonl left
untouched in the tree) - deliberately no persistent golden, because tasks 204-211 grow index.jsonl/catalog and
a pinned matcher output would break on their merges (PITFALLS entry). Result: check on the real files exits 0
(2271 rows, 173 pass = 38 hand_tied + 135 book, 0 fail, 2098 no-tie); the sample verdicts are unchanged (golden
intact); suite 12/12.

## 2026-10-10 200 DECISION: the P180 live route was broken (HTML scraping); replaced with a batched API route (local M<pageid> items, normalized-global chase), P6216 excluded
Where: fit/evidence.py (fetch_page_ids, fetch_file_entities, live_evidence, record_live; fetch_file_item and the UA constant deleted), the depicts bullet of the module docstring, check_depicts
Probing before the first live run (per the iteration-12 plan) showed the old fetch_file_item was wrong in
two ways: (1) the item-QID patterns (ItemPage/(Q\d+), "wikibaseItem", "globalItem") match nothing, because
old file pages carry only a LOCAL MediaInfo entity - the page's mw.config has "wbEntityId":"M<page id>"
(M37646731 for the probe file) and the embedded JSON is that local entity's statements; (2) the P180|P6216
regex matched P6216 *license* statements (Q19652 "public domain") and reported them as depicts values, and
the only Q ids in the page at all were Q13414952 (MD5 - a P459 qualifier on the file's hash statement) and
the license. So the route would have mis-recorded licenses as depictions and never found a real file item.
Fix, verified with live probes: fetch_page_ids (action=query prop=info, 50/batch) gives the page id;
fetch_file_entities then calls the Commons API wbgetentities with ids=M<pid> (the "site" parameter is
rejected by the API but unnecessary; the local wiki returns the entity under "statements", not "claims")
in batches of 50, and for pages whose local entity normalizes to a global item ({"normalized":{"item":"Q…"}}
+ missing) it chases that Q id through the Wikidata service. Only P180 is read as a depiction; P6216 was
also removed from check_depicts (it is a license, never a depicts). The recorded "file_qid" is the item id
actually used (M for local, Q for global). The probe files had no P180 at all, which foreshadowed the
corpus-wide result (next entry).

## 2026-10-10 200 DECISION: record --live batched + chunked; full run recorded all 1338 rows in one session - boxes 1 and 3 verified, task done
Where: fit/evidence.py (record, record_live, live_evidence, resolve_places), data/commons/files.jsonl, tasks/200-evidence.md, tasks/801-evidence-no-tie-coverage.md
Chose batched prefetch + chunked flush over the old per-row fetching: the old record_live_row did
categories/claims/entities/HTML per row (1338 x 4+ requests, hours, and an all-or-nothing rewrite at the
end). Now record_live prefetches once for all pending rows (file categories 50/batch, site claims 50/batch
for 164 unique qids, page ids 50/batch, file entities 50/batch, place searches per unique name with one
batched claims fetch, subcats lazily per site category and cached across rows) and computes each row's
evidence offline from that context (live_evidence - no network in the row loop), flushing files.jsonl in
chunks of 25 so an interrupted run keeps progress (a rerun skips rows on rec == "evidence/1"). The full run
took well under an hour, hit no 429s (commons.get's Retry-After backoff stood by unused), and finished:
825 category, 164 caption_coords, 38 hand_tied (earlier), 354 none (74 with stored conflicts, 280 plain
no-tie). Result: every one of the 1381 titled commons rows + all 890 book rows carries evidence with
specifics and a checked date (box 1); check exits 0 (1162 pass / 0 fail / 1109 no-tie) with the 74
conflict rows stored none-with-conflict, never pass (box 3, real-data confirmation; the sample golden
pins the same behaviour). 1343 lines of files.jsonl changed vs HEAD, every one byte-preserving with
evidence the only and last key added; 147 lines untouched; books file byte-identical; 12/12 tests.
Measured corpus fact: the depicts kind has 0 hits - no site item lists any of these files in P3311/P18
(those files are in the category too and take the category kind first) and no file item depicts the
site's item; the route stays implemented and is pinned by the sample golden (a PASS and a FAIL P180
row). The 280 plain no-tie rows (mostly OS-sheet maps) are the coverage gap the acceptance wording
allows; follow-up filed as tasks/801 (Depends on: 200, Touches: fit/evidence.py).

## 2026-10-11 203a DECISION: the 001 gate is a pure-statistics one-shot - R1 resolved, adapter is thin
The prep notes (R1) inferred an ink/DEM conjunct gate; the MERGED 001 is different: fit_gate.gate(pairs,
transform=None) -> (verdict, stats {n, med, slope_o, io}) - numpy only, no images, no network
(docs/gate.md s.2). So the batch needs no fail-closed gate inputs, no DEM, no old-map ink. The adapter
fit/batch_us.py gate_placement solves plan_fit.similarity from the model's pairs, scores the claimed
placement against the recorded anchors, and records the gate's median residual (m) as the doc's score.
Caveat (by design, docs/gate.md s.7): when the placement is the least-squares fit of the same pairs the
gate sees ~0 residuals ("true case"); it rejects degenerate/nan anchor sets (n<3, no radial spread) and a
claimed placement inconsistent with its anchors. The real check on the auto fits is the human's 18/20
sample - the report lists every auto doc's median for that.

elsewhere is untouched, and the pilot writes nothing):

   misfire "not trusted" on a TRUE answer. Now `implied = abs(a) * k` (the magnitude IS the
   scale): the same rotated fit gives exactly ratio 1.000, no misfire. The NaN guard is unchanged.

## 2026-10-11 204 DECISION: stage() order fixed - the date/date_commons swap runs BEFORE commons.keep() (the sources.py pattern); sanity runs green; lead doc's NL and collection sections written

raised on the Sluis 1980 RCE-album reproduction: stage() evaluated commons.keep() on the RAW page metadata
before the known-drawing-date swap, and keep() judges via year_of() from m["date"] (1980 > MAX_YEAR 1925 ->
drop). The pattern it was copied from (sources.py run()) swaps first and gates second: the done Zwolle row is
the proof (date "circa 1560", date_commons "1980", the same album family) - a post-1925 reproduction of a

before keep(), with the comment); the Rotterdam TOWNS comment was corrected too (the page's date is the

## 2026-10-11 204 DECISION: cat_chain fixed for the current MediaWiki (prop=categories, fail-loud on warnings) + 60-fetch cap + CHAINS table - 56 walks launched
The first `--chain` probe of the long run (Ghent / Brussels / Luxembourg City) exposed a broken walker: `cat_chain`
fetched a category's parents with `action=query&prop=categoryinfo&cicategories=1&ciclimit=500`, but the current
MediaWiki API does not recognize those parameters (response carries `warnings.main.*: "Unrecognized parameters:
cicategories, ciclimit."` - and `commons.get` returns the body without surfacing the warning). So every walk saw
ZERO parents and silently "failed" in ~1 s per town (even Ghent, which the 2026-10-10 prep measured as holding at
4 hops). Two fixes in fit/src_van_deventer.py (my own file):
- **`prop=categories` + `cllimit=500`** for a category page's CONTAINING categories (verified live: Ghent's van
  Deventer category returns '16th-century maps of Ghent' + 'Maps by Jacob van Deventer'), plus a fail-loud guard:
  any response with `error` or `warnings` -> SystemExit. The silent zero-parents degradation is exactly the case
  prep R7 warned about ("the walk is the verification" - a walk that fetches nothing verifies nothing).
- **`CHAIN_FETCH_CAP = 60` per walk + per-level progress lines** (the transcript gets `level k: queue N, next M,
  fetches F` per town). Measured chains are 3-5 hops and a few dozen fetches (Ghent holds at 38), but the BFS
  expands ALL parents, so a disambiguated p373 the map tree does not hold within 6 hops explodes the frontier
  (Brussels (municipality): 730 s and the full 6-level frontier pre-fix, still no hit - genuinely absent, the map
  tree uses the plain 'Brussels' name). The cap bounds that town to ~a minute and sends it to the caption route.
  Refinement found by the probe: when the target was added to the visited set by a REAL fetch before the cap
  stopped the pop loop, the `via[target]` path is fully walked (every edge was returned by an API response), so
  it is returned when it is within the depth cap - that is how Luxembourg City's 4-hop chain is recovered from a
  capped walk. The final message now distinguishes "sits N hops out, beyond the depth cap" / "capped at 60
  fetches" / "no chain within 6 hops".
- **The recording home moved from an inline TOWNS "chain" key to a module-level `CHAINS` table** (the stub comment
  after TOWNS that existed for exactly this) plus a `chain_of(town)` helper used by `evidence_for` and `stage`.
  Rationale: the read tool has not been byte-faithful on this .py file (PITFALLS) and 56 multi-line dict edits
  would be fragile; one mechanical table is reviewable. TOWNS header comment, the cat_chain docstring and the
  stub comment all document the new home; an inline "chain" is still honoured (chain_of checks it first).
Probe results (post-fix, capped): Ghent HOLDS 4 hops via 'Historical images of Ghent' (a different middle than the
prep's 'Maps of Ghent' - both real, this is the actually-walked one); Luxembourg City HOLDS 4 hops via
'Geography of Luxembourg City'; Brussels CAPPED -> caption route (file title names the town). The full 56-town
walk runs in the background (transcript /tmp/vd_chains_iter55.txt, PID file /tmp/vd_chains_iter55.pid); the CHAINS
table gets filled from the transcript's `record:` lines next session after an eyeball pass of every path against
its P373.

```python
inv = []
used = set()
problems = []
for k, v, rs in R:
    hits = [t for t in rows if k in t and t not in used]
    if not hits:
        problems.append(f"rule matches nothing: {k}")
    for t in hits:
        if t in used:
            problems.append(f"double-assigned: {t!r} by rule {k!r}")
        used.add(t)
        inv.append((t, rows[t]["w"], rows[t]["h"], v, rs))
for t in rows:
    if t not in used:
        problems.append(f"UNMATCHED: {t}")
from collections import Counter
vc = Counter(x[3] for x in inv)
print("verdict counts:", dict(vc), "total:", len(inv))
for p in problems:
    print("PROBLEM:", p)
for t, w, h, v, rs in inv:
    if v == "staged" and max(w, h) < 1000: problems.append(f"staged but small: {t}")
    if v == "drop: too small" and max(w, h) >= 1000: problems.append(f"too-small but big: {t}")
if problems:
    raise SystemExit(1)

def q(s):
    return repr(s)
lines = [f"    ({q(t)}, {w}, {h}, {q(v)}, {q(rs)})," for t, w, h, v, rs in sorted(inv)]
block = "INVENTORY = [\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n]\n"
path = "fit/src_kip.py"
src = open(path).read()
old = 'INVENTORY = []  # filled by the first live run (session 1); every title of the lead categories, once'
assert src.count(old) == 1
src = src.replace(old, block)
old_doc = "(an empty INVENTORY only lists - the first run builds it)"
assert src.count(old_doc) == 1
src = src.replace(old_doc, "(the committed 132-row table; a renamed, re-filed or replaced file fails loud)")
open(path, "w").write(src)
print("spliced into", path)
```

- Live re-run (`.venv/bin/python fit/src_kip.py --list --out /tmp/kip_inventory.jsonl`): 132 files, 10 s, no 429 - census unchanged from 2026-10-10/11.

No harm: the INVENTORY replace happened in memory before the failing assert and the file is only written at the end, so the module on disk was untouched. **Fix:** patch the generator to match the two-line wrap and rewrite it as "INVENTORY (the committed 132-row table; a renamed, re-filed or replaced file fails loud)"; re-ran - spliced cleanly.

### 2026-10-11 206 DECISION: the p.212 plan is printed NORTH-UP (page top = north), not north-left as the arrow suggests; the surviving ring is the C11 motte
    Two findings from measuring the fetched page against the ground (details in the task hand-over): (1) The book's p.212 drawing (pentagon, five towers, hall, dashed building, gate) sits in the page's top-left quadrant (bbox ~(10,0)-(425,425) of the 839x840 frame). The only clear surviving ring on the LiDAR/aerial is a ~40 m ditched mound at (E +0..+11 m, N -46..-48 m) from the catalog point - the size and ditch match the C11 MOTTE (Gatehouse 212: 40x20 m hexagonal mound, 25 m ditch), not a 12 m castle tower. With the three reliable anchors (plan hall -> the bright building cluster NW of centre; plan dashed building -> the speck W; plan T4 (bottom horseshoe) -> the motte) the solved similarity under the printed orientation (page left = N, per the arrow) is rotated ~90 deg off the ground, while under north-up it comes out with rotation ~0 deg, scale ~0.41 m/px, the pentagon's south corner due south on the motte and the hall on the NW building: the plan is a normal north-up map and the printed left-pointing arrow is 90 deg off (or marks something else - /tmp/arrow_crop.jpg, 4x zoom of page (170,235)-(345,290), to be re-read; /tmp may be gone). CAVEAT recorded for the fit: with exactly 3 pairs any similar triangle fits both conventions to ~0 residual (6 eqs, 4 params) - the final doc needs >= 4 pairs so the gate is not degenerate.

### 2026-10-11 206 DECISION: the book's own V2 text identifies the plate's castle (OQ-3 resolved); the plan is the 1600 Randle Holme drawing, a pentagon with SIX towers, five drawn
    Re-downloaded the V2 OCR (archive.org castlesofengland02mack: hocr searchtext/pageindex + page_numbers; the page_numbers file is format v2 {identifier, format-version, confidence, pages:[{leafNum, pageNumber}]} and pageindex rows are [leafStart, leafEnd, textStart, textEnd] - the prep's "leaf->printed map" guess was wrong). The Shotwick chapter (printed p.180, running head CHESHIRE 181 on the continuation page; next chapter STOCKPORT) says: the plan is "a drawing and plan of this fortress by Kendle [Randle] Holme, as it appeared then, in a ruinous condition. Its trace was a pentagon strengthened by six towers, one of which, according to Camden, was five storeys high", and of the 1897 remains: "those seen at present consisting merely of a large mound, supported by a huge earthwork of crescent form, and two deep entrenchments on the land side". The index reads "Shotlack, ii. 179, Shotwick, ii. 180". So the p.212 plate (leaf 212 = printed 164; the Lancaster plate leaf 231 = printed 183, 19 pages on) is a plan of Shotwick drawn from Holme's c.1600 depiction of the ruined fortress - which explains the five (of six) towers, the thick bank, and why the modern ground only carries the motte + crescent + entrenchments. This is the backbone of docs/lead_mackenzie.md section 3 (evidence chain a-f) and of the fit's expectations.

# Task 212 cover-final

## 2026-10-12 212 DECISION: fit/cover.py designed - six phases on an injectable root, the live run later
The task's loop, search and sync become one module, fit/cover.py (new; its tests tests/test_cover.py).
Design settled after reading site_done.py, matchfit.py, batch_us.run_sites, review.upsert_item/export,
commons (search/files_of/keep/info/thumbs/classify), fit/evidence.record, plan_fit, export_plans and
serve.after_write. Phases (each takes root, so a test drives them on a temp tree; a CLI runs them in
order, `all`, with --root and --working/--model-json like site_done):

1. fetch(root): local copies before export_plans (the lead's second point). Files with a `thumb`
   missing their local jpg: fetch the 1280 thumb (commons.thumbs' behaviour: .part->rename, 1/s pace,
   resumable - re-implemented here with a root parameter; commons.thumbs itself is bound to the
   checkout's module-level RAW/OUT). Files with only a `url` (the ORL/Limes rows, 54): commons.info(
   [title]) gives the 1280 thumburl (imageinfo iiurlwidth=1280) - fetch that; fall back to the raw
   url (utm-stripped) when info has no thumb. Then regenerate web/data/plans.json with
   export_plans.main() (in-process; its ROOT/BOOKS and commons' OUT/RAW are module constants - a
   temp-tree test monkeypatches them, that is setup, not product behaviour). Measured on the synced
   tree (main a858f48): 131 classified rows missing a local copy (ALL meet the plans threshold
   p_photo<0.5 and max(p_plan,p_birdseye)>=0.3, none in plans yet -> plans.json grows 1168 -> ~1299,
   matching the lead's Mac 1296); 401 thumb rows missing locally; 54 url-only rows (1 has a copy).
   The 211 rows are ALREADY classified (all 930 classified rows are in files.jsonl) - no classifier
   needed for them, only copies.
2. search(root): for every BUILT site with no fit (no doc and drawings 0 - recomputed after phase 1,
   so sites that just gained candidates drop out of the set) and no plans.json candidate: with a qid -
   (a) its P373 category via commons.wd_claims, files with commons.files_of(cat, depth=1); (b) P180 -
   evidence.fetch_page_ids + fetch_file_entities on every title gathered so far, keep the ones whose
   MediaInfo depicts the qid (the proven path, not a new API); (c) the title search
   commons.search(name) (its 3 full-text queries). Without a qid: (c) only, and the record says so.
   Keep with commons.keep (1925 cut-off, no regex); dedupe against files.jsonl titles. Per site the
   SEARCH RECORD names exactly what ran: the category (name or "none"), the file counts, the qid
   queried for P180 (or "no qid"), the 3 title queries, the date, and any route that failed (a
   429/timeout is recorded, not hidden - the record must be true).
3. stage(root): newly found files -> files.jsonl (harvest row shape + qid + by:"212") + local copy
   (phase 1's fetcher) + classified.jsonl via an INJECTABLE classifier (default the clef batch,
   commons.classify's questions) + the 200 evidence field via evidence.record(files, books, live,
   only=new sites) (live in the working phase; a stub in tests) + export_plans again (growth-only).
4. loop(root, model=None): the normal loop, and the FIT IS THE MATCHER (see next entry). For every
   built site that still has no fit, run site_done.main([sid, --root root]) in-process WITHOUT
   --working: matchfit.run (ELoFTR 8091; RoMa 8092 is down on this VM and skipped automatically)
   writes a doc (fitter:"matcher") for every picture it is sure of, including ones already in a
   review item (a confident matcher fit resolves the item); the rest get batch_us.run_sites'
   upsert ("no model answer" when model=None) into the item; a site with zero candidates gets the
   batch's no_picture item, which phase 5 re-records with the exact searched string. site_done
   already syncs each new doc (line check: agent docs get the matcher's spread guard, not the
   batch-model ladder clause), refreshes drawings, and scopes the review export to the site.
   --working (the vision model, 301) is NEVER passed by 212: it invented points and must not place.
5. nopicture(root): every search-set site that ends with no candidates and no fit gets
   review.upsert_item(root, sid, [], no_picture={searched: <exact record>, at}) - entries=[] + a
   dict keeps any existing candidates (verified in upsert_item: the dict branch wins; candidates are
   merged, never cleared) and rewrites the batch's generic "plans.json (N rows, ...)" searched string
   with the exact one. A site whose search routes all failed gets the item too, with the failures
   recorded - box 6's invariant (every built site: drawings >= 1 OR an open item) holds even when
   the network lies.
6. sync(root) + export(root) + report(root): sync = the page-facing sync (box 3), a plan_fit sweep
   over EVERY doc but per-doc proof: plan_fit.main's own loop only catches SystemExit per doc (the
   serve worker catches the WHOLE sweep and gives up, serve.py ~line 261-273), so cover owns the
   loop and imports plan_fit's primitives (who_placed, is_done, build, prune, NO_PROVENANCE): per
   doc, hand -> build with no check; agent -> build; unmarked auto -> stamp by:agent then build;
   no provenance -> refuse (item entry); ANY other exception -> record the failure, continue, and
   upsert that site's item with the build-failure reason (so the invariant holds when an overlay
   cannot be built). prune at the end (the deleted docs' overlays). export = review.export(root)
   full (box 4, the one and only writer of web/data/review.json). report = docs/batch.md (box 5) in
   batch_us.write_report's shape but FINAL over all built sites: counts per outcome (fit hand = the
   golden 21, fit automatic = every by:agent doc (batch + matcher + line-saved), human-saved =
   by:hand docs outside the golden 21, review item, no picture found), the 20-sample of
   automatically accepted fits drawn from the WHOLE auto-doc union with 212's OWN recorded seed
   SEED_212 = 20261012 (batch 20261010, null 20261011 - the date convention) and page URL + gate
   score per pick, and the no-picture list with each site's exact searched record.

Tests (tests/test_cover.py, no network, port 0): temp tree (conftest pattern: web/ + data/ copied,
per-site web dirs, stand-in pictures PIL-drawn to the doc's size) seeded with a matcher doc, a
golden hand doc, an unmarked auto doc, a no-provenance doc and a bad-commons doc; monkeypatched
(setup, not product): the commons/evidence network getters (recorded titles/metadata), the
classifier (recorded p_*), matchfit.reachable/run (a recorded confident fit and the unreachable
case), export_plans' ROOT/BOOKS and commons' OUT/RAW (the temp root). Drive the phases in-process,
then check through the SERVED page (the served fixture, port 0): every built site in the served
sites.json has drawings >= 1 or is in the served review.json open list (box 6, the GOAL point 1 in
full); the 000 golden test re-runs unchanged (the 21 hand docs and 19 site.json stay byte-identical -
verified separately with sha256sum -c after every live run); the docs/batch.md sample equals
random.Random(SEED_212).sample(sorted auto-doc ids, 20) recomputed in the test (fixed, reproducible
- the human's 18/20 check depends on it). State-aware per the 203b pitfall: the test computes its
expected sets from the temp tree's live docs/items, never from pinned counts (agent c's 302a/304/306
drift the live store in parallel).

## 2026-10-12 212 DECISION: the loop's fit is the matcher, never the vision model (the lead, ef84a05)
The lead note (commit ef84a05, merged into this branch 2026-10-12) steers the task: the fit in 212's
loop is the MATCHER via tools/site_done.py, never a vision-model fit. Rationale recorded by the
lead: the vision-model batch fit invented its points (301) and must not place anything; an unsure
matcher result goes to the review item, as site_done already does. Evidence on this VM (measured
this session): ELoFTR on 127.0.0.1:8091 answers /health (matchanything_eloftr on the RTX 5060 Ti)
so matchfit.reachable() is TRUE here - the matcher pass will actually run in the working phase;
RoMa on 8092 does not answer (matchfit.run skips its second pass when it is down, by design).
Consequently 212's loop runs site_done WITHOUT --working and WITHOUT --model-json (model=None):
the matcher places what it is sure of (>= 10 inliers, rotation within 30 deg, spread guard -
matchfit.judge); the rest land in the review item as "no model answer" (batch_us.run_sites'
upsert, the path site_done already uses). This supersedes the iteration-200 hand-over plan that
had the loop on batch_us.llm_model (the AI-box LLM on 8081 does answer, but it is the 301 fabricator
and the lead forbids it for placement). The vision model may still be used nowhere in 212: not for
placement, and not as a classifier substitute without a human decision (see next entry).

## 2026-10-11 213 DECISION: the prep's Imola "centre 44.245 N, 12.367 E / bad P625 53 km NW" was wrong - that point is Cervia; P625 is the correct city point
The prep notes placed Imola's old town at 44.245 N, 12.367 E and, seeing Q50195's P625 (44.353, 11.715) far
from it, called the P625 "bad, ~53 km NW of the town". Verified live (2026-10-11): the prep point is CERVIA
on the Ravenna coast (~50 km SE of Imola); the real city is at 44.353 N, 11.715 E, where THREE independent
sources agree: the enwiki infobox (44°21'11"N 11°42'53"E), Wikidata P625, and the OSM town node (with the F1
circuit beside it and the Santerno - "Fiume Santerno" at 44.3606/11.7104 - running through the urban area).
So the "53 km trap" was the distance between two wrong values. Consequences: (a) the site point is the
walled town's centre, 11.7112/44.3535 (Piazza del Duomo, OSM) - the centre of the sheet's circular view, not
the modern city point; (b) the prep's "Savena crossing" was a second error - the drawing's river is the
Santerno, which Leonardo labels "Sant'Arno" (mirror script, read off the sheet); the view is south-up per
the literature; (c) the evidence story changes: for Imola the live record route resolves the RIGHT QID (the
hand record still stands to pin the walled centre, deterministic and offline); the name-search trap that is
REAL and documented is Venice (first hit with P625 = Q773853 Venice, California, 9891 km). Side note: OSM's
comune boundary for Imola is mis-drawn (Nominatim displays the urban area as "Imola, Nuovo Circondario
Imolese", and the admin relation's centre sits 8 km north of the city) - a reason never to geocode Imola
from OSM/Nominatim. The PITFALLS entry "Q50195 (Imola) carries a bad P625..." must be corrected accordingly
(pending in the next session; I cannot edit PITFALLS from the context-limit hand-over step).

## 2026-10-12 219 DECISION: 302c no longer blocks - the lead dropped 302c/302d in main d39ead8
The task's `Depends on: 302c` existed only because both touched pipeline/plan_fit.py. The lead's
commit d39ead8 (main, 2026-10-12) dropped 302c/302d as superseded by the matcher fit and set 219's
Depends line to `none`. 302c never made its design changes to plan_fit.py (its own hand-over:
investigation only, no code), so nothing from it collides with 219's edit; plan_fit.py is
byte-identical between my branch and main (merge-base e2ca3d9; main's only commit since is d39ead8,
task files + journals only). Proceeded on this branch without waiting.

## 2026-10-12 219 DECISION: year-once rule = drop the label parenthesis whenever the title carries any 4-digit year
The task's two sentences ("drop the label's parenthesis when the title already contains that year"
vs "only a title without a year shows the label (or 'undated')") diverge for the 3 docs whose
label-year differs from the title-year (argentoratum 1831/1836, bethlehem 1881/1882, mound-bottom
1923/1924). Implemented the stricter, unambiguous one: the parenthesis appears ONLY for a yearless
title (label or "undated"); a titled year always drops it. The label is not lost from the page: it
stays in the entry's `scale` field. The year check reuses the same 4-digit pattern as the entry's
sort year (_year4) so the two can never disagree; non-4-digit numbers ("116", "0154", 5-digit ids,
"17th century") are not years, so "(1750-1900)"-style labels still show under yearless titles.

## 2026-10-12 219 DECISION: refactor source_line extraction is byte-identical for all 133 store docs
Extracted the citation + who/how clause from build() into pure source_line(doc, n, m, who) and the
year regex into _year4 (committed 4b93f5c). Proof: a throwaway script evaluated the old inline
expressions (copied verbatim from HEAD) and the new function for every doc in data/db/platefits
(133) with m from similarity(doc['pairs']) unscaled - 0 mismatches. The least-squares similarity is
scale-equivariant (scaling all u,v by the picture's fs scales a back by 1/fs, leaving the ground
residuals the same), so m and corners do not depend on which image size stands in for the picture;
this is why the hermetic test can build with a stand-in image of the doc's own frame size (fs=1)
and still pin the exact how-clause.

## 2026-10-12 219 DECISION: re-bake = plan_fit.build per stale entry, then restore sites.json byte-for-byte
The one-off re-bake (14 built year-titled commons depictions + shotwick, which had never been
built in this checkout) ran the product's own path: plan_fit.build(doc) per doc, root = this
checkout. Contrary to the previous hand-over's expectation, every big picture was already
cached in data/raw/commons/big/ -> zero downloads. Proof that "only the string changes": for
all 14 the rebuilt entry equals the stored one in every field except source; a second
identical run is byte-stable (the fixed state is a fixed point); shotwick's rebuilt entry
matches agent a's built entry (corners, fit, year, label, scale, coverage, kind, file, ink)
with only the source fixed. Each build's trailing build_site.set_drawings refreshed
web/data/sites.json (tracked, in 306's Touches) - the committed bookkeeping was stale (5
sites: drawings 0 despite built plans, bethlehem 0->12) - and I restored the committed
bytes: a gitignored build does not change committed bookkeeping (agent a's checkout follows
the same convention); the product refreshes the file on its own next time. The naive
verification check ("(label)" in source) false-positives on 3 of the 15 (avaricum, bolsover,
castle-rising: the label string occurs inside the title itself) - the structural test is
source.split(", Wikimedia Commons:")[0] == title (PITFALLS).

```
def test_sources_filter_merges_only_named_sources(tmp_path):
    """--sources scopes a run to one source family (230's Roman re-run must not fold in the US families'
    still-pending staging, whose own consolidation is 236c): only the named families' rows enter the
    canonical files and the log, and the later unfiltered rerun picks up the rest exactly once."""
    tree = tmp_path / "aw"
    (tree / "fit").mkdir(parents=True)
    (tree / "data/catalog").mkdir(parents=True)
    (tree / "data/merge").mkdir(parents=True)
    shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(ROOT, "fit", "merge.py"), tree / "fit" / "merge.py")

    def row(**kw):
        return json.dumps(kw, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"

    (tree / "data/catalog/extras.jsonl").write_text(row(id="x0", name="Old"))
    (tree / "data/catalog/extras_a.jsonl").write_text(row(id="xa", name="A"))
    (tree / "data/catalog/extras_b.jsonl").write_text(row(id="xb", name="B"))

    p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "fit/merge.py", "merge", "--root", ".", "--sources", "b"],
                       cwd=str(tree), capture_output=True, text=True)
    assert p.returncode == 0, p.stderr + p.stdout
    extras = open(tree / "data/catalog/extras.jsonl").read()
    assert '"xb"' in extras and '"xa"' not in extras, "the filter must merge only the named source"
    log = [json.loads(l) for l in _lines(str(tree / "data/merge/log.jsonl"))]
    assert log and all(e["source"] == "b" for e in log), "the log records the filtered run only"

    p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "fit/merge.py", "merge", "--root", "."],
                       cwd=str(tree), capture_output=True, text=True)
    assert p.returncode == 0, p.stderr + p.stdout
    extras = open(tree / "data/catalog/extras.jsonl").read()
    assert '"xa"' in extras and extras.count('"xb"') == 1, "the unfiltered rerun picks up the rest, once"
```

Retained B tree (pytest-0/awowner0) timeline: doc write 01:57:15.802, base overlay :16.816, ink overlay :23.309, **depictions.json :23.310, sites.json :23.429 (119 ms), review.json :23.846**. web/index.html `saveFit()` polls depictions.json every 1.5 s and, when the saved depiction appears, fetches sites.json ONCE, adopts drawings/score/oldest/overlays and sets the marker class from that one fetch, then stops. A poll landing in the 119 ms gap adopts the pre-rescore score and the marker keeps its old tier until a manual reload (the owner would see the wrong square tier). B's poll landed in the gap (t1 adopted); A's landed after the re-score (t2 adopted) - hence the per-save flake. **Suite run 1 (the branch as it stood at it.236, no changes yet):** 1 failed, 183 passed, 1 skipped in 585.97 s (`/tmp/loop-ancient-works.a/fullsuite-237.log`). All four a423d19 reds green (matchfit 2/2; owner_check pair green; test_merge, test_data, serve, all src_ tests green). The single red: tests/test_src_roman_maclauchlan.py::test_check_staged_joins_and_passes at step (a): `join: staged site luguvallium-q71551754 differs from its canonical row in extras.jsonl` (check_staged() returned 1, `assert 1 == 0`). Not in the a423d19 failure list and not in any loop-start note, so a NEW failure on this branch - and, being a date-bomb, unfixable by waiting (it reds on every day after the merge date).

**Root cause (measured, not guessed):** the test's first step re-runs the book's stage() into temp files (offline), then check_staged() joins the freshly staged row against the REAL canonical files (monkeypatched to temp copies of them only in steps b/c). stage() built the site row with `"checked": now()` and the picture row with `evidence: {"checked": now(), ...}` where `now()` = `time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")` = the run date. The committed staging rows (207b, staged 2026-10-14) and the canonical rows 230 merged from them (byte-identical copies) carry 2026-10-14 - the day the LIVE verification actually ran: the P625 cross-check ("(verified 2026-10-14)") and the sitelinks check (the note field hard-codes "(sitelinks checked 2026-10-14)"). A fresh re-stage on 2026-10-15 re-stamps both fields to 2026-10-15; the join normalizes FULL row content (`_canon_norm` = same norm fit/merge.py uses on the merge line), so the fresh row differs from the merged row in exactly two date fields (verified by walking the fresh-vs-canonical row diff: only `location_check.checked` and `evidence.checked` differ) -> "differs" -> exit 1. The test passed in a423d19 only because that run was on 2026-10-14, the same date as the staging/merge -> identical rows. The test itself is correct and was NOT touched: case (b) is exactly the intended post-merge contract ("a merged row is a no-op"), and only a deterministic staging date can satisfy it on later days. An offline re-stage that has not re-run the live checks must not claim a new verification date - that is what re-stamping does, and it is a false record under the 200 evidence contract either way.

**Fix (fit/src_roman_maclauchlan.py added to 230's Touches line this session - the it.216 precedent: the 230 merge is what made the row canonical and thereby exposed the re-stamp, so 230 fixes it):** `now()` and the `time` import replaced by a stored constant `CHECKED = "2026-10-14"` (commented: the day the live verification ran; an offline re-stage must not re-stamp it, because the merged canonical row carries it and a re-stamped row differs on any later day, 230 it.237); both `"checked": now()` sites now use it; `_norm`'s docstring corrected (the dates no longer vary with the staging date). Committed staging files and canonical files UNCHANGED (they already carry 2026-10-14; stage() is idempotent and writes no byte on a populated file). Verified: test_src_roman_maclauchlan 4/4 in 4.2 s (offline, socket-blocked, temp trees); the module's own `--check` CLI exits 0 on the real post-merge tree ("evidence: 1 rows, 1 pass, 0 fail, 0 no-tie", no join: lines). # Task 300 site-stonehenge

## 2026-10-11 300 DECISION: the one-site line (tools/site_done.py) reuses batch_us.run_sites only for UNCOVERED candidates, and needs three root-aware refactors (plan_fit, build_site, scoped review.export)
Where: tools/site_done.py (new), pipeline/plan_fit.py, pipeline/build_site.py, fit/review.py
Rationale: measured state - Stonehenge's 13 plans.json rows all have a verdict (7 auto docs, 6 in its
review item, sets disjoint), so running run_sites blindly (even model=None) would not fit anything new
but its write_item upsert would REPLACE the 6 rich batch-written candidate entries (gate scores, model
pairs, why) with "no model answer" stubs (upsert merges by whole-entry replacement, PITFALLS fit/).
So site_done's fit step runs run_sites only when a candidate has neither doc nor item entry (or the
site has no candidates at all, no pre-fit and no item - the no-picture case). The existing steps were
not root-aware: plan_fit and build_site derive every path from their own file location, and
review.export records the write-once resolved field into EVERY derivably-resolved item (today exactly
one other site: alligator-effigy-mound-q4732645) - a one-site command must not touch other sites'
files, hence export(root, site_id=None) (scoped record, same page file) and _root(root=None) threading
through plan_fit (build/main/prune/load_picture + new is_done) and build_site (drawings/set_drawings/
write_entry). serve.py calls plan_fit.main([]) - default args must stay behaviour-identical.
Also fixed in plan_fit while in there: the `how` string claims "Placed by hand" for automatic fits
(wrong on the public page; auto docs get "Fitted automatically by the batch ... (gate score X m)",
hand-fit strings unchanged), and load_picture's bare urllib has no Wikimedia pacing/Retry-After
(7 back-to-back downloads 429, PITFALLS ~L602) - new _fetch helper paces ~1 rps, honours Retry-After,
backoffs on 5xx. Baseline before all changes: 59 passed / 0 failed (59.76 s). Not yet implemented at
hand-over: the design is fully specced in the task's Hand-over; next session writes the code, then the
real run (7 Commons downloads expected), then a re-run for idempotency, then tests/browser/docs.

## 2026-10-11 300 DECISION: the one-site line is implemented and has taken Stonehenge to the map; one session remains (tests/test_site_done.py)
Where: tools/site_done.py (new), pipeline/plan_fit.py, pipeline/build_site.py, fit/review.py, docs/site_flow.md, docs/site_flow/stonehenge.png, web/data/{sites.json,review.json,sites/stonehenge-q39671/}, data/raw/commons/big/
Rationale: iteration 65 implemented exactly the previous session's design and ran the line on the real
`tree with no model flag. Results, all verified on disk: (1) fit - "13 candidate picture(s): 7 fitted (doc),
6 in the review item -> no batch run needed" (the covered/uncovered distinction worked: run_sites was never

## 2026-10-11 300 DECISION: tests/test_site_done.py runs the copied one-site line on a copy of Stonehenge's files with a socket-dead subprocess and big pictures at the REAL cache dimensions; task done
Where: tests/test_site_done.py (new)
Rationale: box 4, the last box. The test builds a throwaway tree in tmp_path: the code copied whole
(tools/, fit/, pipeline/ - site_done resolves its data root from its own path, so the copied code runs on
the copied data), all of web/data/{sites.json (stonehenge's drawings zeroed to pre-sync), plans.json,
review.json}, data/review/ (all 340 items) and data/db/platefits/ (all 130 docs), and the site dir minus its
14 plan webps with depictions.json stripped to its 2 maps. The 7 Commons big pictures the sync would
otherwise download are seeded as flat-colour JPEGs at the EXACT real cache dimensions (headers read through
the checkout's committed data/raw symlink; the batch tests link the same store) - one twist vs the iter 65
design, which assumed fs=1: 3 of the 7 big files are 1.19-1.75x the doc's `size` and m_per_px in
depictions.json depends on that factor (now a PITFALLS entry under pipeline/); the fit math is
content-free, so only the dimensions matter and depictions.json comes out byte-identical to the repo's.
The subprocess guard is `sys.executable -c GUARD tree/tools/site_done.py stonehenge-q39671`: GUARD kills
socket.socket.connect/connect_ex and socket.create_connection, then runpy.run_path(run_name="__main__") -

The batch's three pre-gate counterchecks all pass BY CONSTRUCTION on this class: the stated-scale cross-check compares the model's stated scale with its own ladder's implied scale (they agree by construction), and _feature_present passes because ladder points scattered over structureless Salisbury Plain sit at/above the 400-point null median (the next-door candidate c_ffb3d drew the 25% verdict). A model (duck-typed: .boxes(im) -> 0-1000-normalised non-map boxes, .label_pieces(im, pieces) -> per-piece kind) may blank non-map boxes and keep only wall-labelled pieces; an absent/unusable answer falls back to the no-model rule and is labelled as such in the result.
- Seed: fit/propose.propose_for (scale bar > ratio at recorded ppi > picture-size; north arrow unless |deg|>60 or unrecorded -> north-up; centre = site centre, i.e. t0 = (0,0) in relief-box-centre metres). Fallback when propose raises (no scale at all): max(size_m)/max(panel px extent), north-up, site centre.

- Objective (selection): mean over template points of max(contrast, -0.2 m); contrast = fit_plate's ridge contrast (relief on the line minus the HIGHER of the two sides side_m away); LRM = aw.local_relief(radius_m 24), clipped +-1.0 m, modern_mask and water_mask set to NaN (fit_plate's defaults; the per-site hand knobs in data/sites/<id>/site.json are hand-fit artefacts and are NEVER read by the method); >= 50% of points on valid relief else score -9.

## 2026-10-11 302a DECISION: placement->similarity geometry verified; b convention is complex(u0c, -v0c) (MINUS-v) - the session-3 script's +v0c was an 860 m near-miss
Session 4: re-ran the session-3 verification script (kept in the iter-0075 log) and found it had a SECOND bug beyond the noted broadcast fix: it applied M to [du, dv] instead of the autofit convention d = [du, -(v - v0)]. With both fixed (d = [u-u0c, -(v-v0c)], en = d @ M.T + t; lon/lat = aw.to_lonlat(cx + e/k, cy + n/k), k = 1/aw.ground_scale(lat)):
- plan_fit.similarity recovers a = k*s*exp(i*rot) to relative error 7e-6 (= the 1 dp px / 7 dp lon-lat rounding limit of the synthetic pairs), residuals 1.4-4.6 mm; fit_gate.gate accepts (med 3 mm).
- **b = (cx + k*tE) + i(cy + k*tN) - a*complex(u0c, -v0c)** — the minus-v form. The session-3 script used complex(u0c, +v0c) and reported a relative error of 1.3e-4, which looked fine only because |b| ~ 6.6e6 m absorbs the 860 m disagreement. Cross-checked both ways: the solved b matches zc - a*complex(u0,-v0) to the rounding limit, and re-fitting propose._anchor_pairs' 5 pairs recovers that anchor's a and b exactly (a = (m_per_px/ground_scale)*e^(i*rot), b = zc - a*complex(u0, -v0)).
fit/inkfit.py's placement_of and map_pairs must use the minus-v w0 and the flipped-v d; the rest of the design stands as recorded in the task file.

## 2026-10-11 302a DECISION: session 6 - the method verified end to end (hermetic + 2 real sites); two bug fixes; boxes 1 and 3 ticked

All parameters still exactly the frozen registration; both fixes below are bug fixes, not tuning.
- BUG FIX (module): template_pieces returned `_keep_pieces(...)` as its first element, but that function returns a (list, label) TUPLE - so fit() received pieces = (list_of_dicts, "") and the iteration blew up with "list indices must be integers or slices, not str" the moment a non-empty piece list was produced. It was masked in session 5 because every run so far had early-returned at "no wall ink extracted" (empty list = falsy). Fixed by unpacking inside template_pieces (kept, label = _keep_pieces(...); return kept, _variant(model) + label, notes).
- BUG FIX (CLI hygiene): the CLI printed the search progress and aw's fetch chatter (overpass retries) to stdout, corrupting the JSON result file. main() now redirects sys.stdout to sys.stderr around the fit() call (print() resolves sys.stdout dynamically, so this catches aw.py's own prints too) and emits only the JSON document on stdout. No changes outside fit/inkfit.py.
- Hermetic run (the /tmp/aw-inkfit-herm/root fixture, recreated this session): the 8 px sharp drawing was NOT the fix - a razor-sharp 0/1 step makes the frozen Frangi (gamma 0.013, calibrated on soft real-scan edges) ghost-echo a ring ~5-8 px OUTSIDE the drawn walls (even inside the zeroed margin), and a blurred 8 px line falls under the ridge threshold. The scan-realistic fixture (8 px rectangle + 12 px interior line, gaussian_filter 2.5 px, +-2/255 paper noise, rng seed 7; 12 px is inside the real 6-20 px wall band) gives exactly the 3 true centre lines, no ghosts. fit() then ran fully offline in 8.1 s: 3 pieces / 81 template points, seed 0.75 (the hermetic picture-size fallback - propose_for has no catalog in the temp root, as designed), search landed on the TRUE placement (s 0.7408, rot -0.5 deg, t [-17, 0] vs true 0.75/0/0), both nulls valid, gate accept (n 6, 4 mm), fabrication silent, doc returned with fitter:"ink" and batch_us's field shape. CONFIDENCE WAS NEGATIVE (-0.025): fit 0.7152 vs scramble 0.7404; the shifted-DEM null was -9 (invalid: shifting the 120x100 m box half its size leaves a 60x40 m valid region smaller than the 120x90 m template - recorded by design, shifted_valid:false). Two toy-geometry lessons for 302c's committed test site: (a) make the site box much larger than the earthwork (a 1000 m-class box with a ~100 m earthwork) so the half-box shift keeps >= 50% of the template valid; (b) a template of one or two long straight pieces keeps scramble signal (a long straight wall re-aligned to any one ridge side still scores) - a fixture with several pieces of different lengths/angles makes the null discriminating. The method ANSWERED "not confident" on the toy site - that is the decision layer working, not a failure.

<!-- task 302c -->
# Task 302c decision-wiring

## 2026-10-12 302c DECISION: the confidence threshold is 0.15, set on the 302b held-out table (box 1) - the null margin only rations the pass rate; it is not an accuracy guarantee
First session on 302c (iteration 84): investigation and design only, no code written (the context
limit hit before the first edit). The value and the design, frozen for the next session:
- Threshold CONF_THRESHOLD = 0.15 on the search-matched-null margin (confidence = objective_fit
  - max(scramble, shifted) as fit/inkfit.py already computes). Rationale from the 302b table
  (docs/site_flow.md "Measured one-shot"): sorted margins run -0.5150..+0.1871 and do NOT
  separate good from bad fits (worst calleva +0.1070/2203.6 m sits above castle-rising +0.0806
  and old-sarum-book +0.0693). A threshold > 0 passes 11 docs, > 0.05 passes 6, > 0.10 passes 2
  (badbury AND the worst, calleva); only a threshold in (0.1070, 0.1871] passes exactly one
  document - badbury, the best (264.5 m, 17% of the site's size). 0.15 is mid-interval: 0.043 of
  room above calleva's rounded 0.1070 and 0.037 below badbury's 0.1871, robust to small DEM/OSM
  drift between the held-out run and a re-run. A future change to the value is a method change:
  it must be labelled and re-measured, never a silent fix.
- Decision (applied in fit/inkfit.py, additive): confident iff the fit produced reportable pairs
  AND the frozen gate accepted them (verdict == fit_gate.ACCEPT) AND fabrication_pattern is
  silent AND the null ran AND margin >= 0.15. Everything else is unsure with a
  human-readable reason (the existing no-fit reasons are already human-readable; new: a gate
  refusal names the median residual; a below-threshold margin names the margin, the fit and
  null objectives and which null won - per the 302a hand-over note). Confident -> automatic
  platefit document (auto: true, fitter: "ink", the gate's score); unsure -> the site's review
  item with the reason and the best starting pairs, never to the map.
- New result fields are "confident" (bool) and "unsure_reason" (str|None). The "reason" field
  keeps its exact meaning (None on the success path): inkfit_heldout.measure() stores r["reason"]
  into the frozen one-shot checkpoint (data/inkfit/heldout/results.json), so routing the margin
  message through "reason" would corrupt the checkpoint if measure were ever re-run. "confident"/
  "unsure_reason" are new keys measure() does not store, so the checkpoint and the verbatim table
  stay untouched (verify: `fit/inkfit_heldout.py table` byte-identical to the committed section).
- Task file: Touches extended to docs/site_flow.md (the decision paragraph goes next to the
table), data/inkfit/ (the committed test-site relief npz seeds under data/inkfit/relief/, the
committed real-plate copies under data/inkfit/plates/) and tests/test_site_done.py (the
no-model CLI message of site_done changes wording, and that test asserts the line verbatim).
Next session: implement box 1 exactly as the hand-over spells it (the decide() contract, the
site_flow.md paragraph text, the verification list incl. applying decide() to the 21 checkpoint
entries -> exactly badbury confident), then box 2 (site_done wiring), 3 (plan_fit.build how
string) and 4 (tests/test_inkfit.py + the committed seeds; badbury = confident e2e, calleva =
unsure e2e).

# Task 302f matcher-station-test

## 2026-10-13 302f DECISION: iteration 210 - investigation only; the fixture is keyed by the sha256 of the exact request body matchfit.match sends, and the test's stub reuses that key, so no image code runs in the stub
    No code written this session (context limit during design; the full trace is in the task
    hand-over). Design decisions taken, so the next session does not re-litigate them:
    - Fixture format (tests/fixtures/matchfit_station/records.json + records_unsure.json):
      {"header": {...}, "responses": {sha256(exact request body): <verbatim live /match JSON>}}.
      matchfit.match sends json.dumps({"image0": b64(PNG of the plan crop), "image1": b64(PNG of
      the ground window), "threshold": 0.2, "max_side": 1024}); the recorder monkeypatches
      urllib.request.urlopen to record (body sha256 -> response) while matchfit.fit_row runs
      live against 127.0.0.1:8091 (twice, for a stability check), and the test's in-process
      stub answers POST /match by the same key. Same .venv PIL (12.3.0) + same source bytes on
      both sides => same PNG bytes => same key; a missing key 500s and the test's stderr==""
      assertion fails loudly. 15 requests per fit_row (3 grounds x 5 windows); RoMa needs no
      responses (ROMA_URL points at a dead ephemeral port; reachable()'s except Exception swallows
      the guard's AssertionError).
    - Unsure variant: deterministic permutation (np.random.default_rng(7)) of the ground-side
      keypoints of every response whose candidate has >= 10 inliers (frozen heldout: six-inch
      x0.5 = 15, x0.35 = 22 - BOTH must be broken, since fit_row's strict-greater best would
      otherwise stay confident on x0.5); the script asserts the perturbed best lands at
      3..9 inliers (frozen values say 8, six-inch x0.7, rot -43.51) and records the exact
      "not sure: N consistent points (need 10)" line in the header; the test asserts that line
      verbatim (N from the header, never hardcoded).
    - GUARD variant: patch socket.socket.connect and connect_ex to pass through only
      (127.0.0.1, stub_port) (allowed port via env GUARD_ALLOW) and raise AssertionError
      otherwise; do NOT patch socket.create_connection to dead (it must flow through to the
      patched instance connect). The test_site_done/test_fit_queue full-dead guard is the
      template.
    - The unsure branch's published review.json must NOT be asserted equal to the repo's
      current web/data/review.json (457 items may have drifted from what export recomputes
      today): the test recomputes the baseline by calling fit/review.py export in-process on a
      second clean tmp copy and expects exactly baseline + the badbury entry (same name sort).
    - Tmp tree inputs (all verified to exist in this checkout): the code dirs tools/ fit/
      pipeline/; web/data/{sites,plans,review}.json; a REAL copy of web/data/sites/badbury...
      (it is a symlink to another checkout - copy os.path.realpath); data/db/platefits (all 70,
      then delete the badbury doc); data/review (all 481); data/books/index.jsonl (evidence +
      propose), data/commons/files.jsonl, data/catalog/sites.jsonl (export's name fallback -
      missing => stderr warning, and the test asserts stderr == ""), data/sites/<SID>/site.json
      (no "plate" field: is_pre_fit False), data/raw/books/earthworkenglan01allcgoog/full/

## 2026-10-12 304 DECISION: re-read passes on the +theta sign convention (no flip); panel_pieces fixed to mirror template_pieces' piece selection so the scramble draws land exactly as 302b's

Session 3. The file was already committed by the driver (3b4c2b2 "[driver] uncommitted
work after iteration 86"); the import check passed clean (no breakage to fix). The
three Re-read items were re-verified with fresh eyes against the source:

1. **Sign convention (CRITICAL item) - passes, no flip.**
   `propose._anchor_pairs` is `z = (m_per_px/k) * e^{i theta} * (w - wc) + zc` with
   `w = u - i v` (page coords, v down) and `z` Mercator (imag = north). A visual
   (on-screen) counterclockwise rotation by phi multiplies the `w = x - i y` frame by
   **+e^{i phi}** (verified: at 90 deg the up vector (0,-1) goes to left (-1,0), which is
   CCW on screen and +i in the w frame). A drawn plan whose north arrow is theta deg
   CLOCKWISE of page-up has the 302b anchor factor e^{i theta}; rotating the panel image
   by **+theta** (PIL `rotate(+deg)` is counterclockwise on screen) brings it north-up.
   So `_match_theta`'s `rotate_image(panel, +theta)` and `rotated_panel_map`'s
   `R = [[c, s], [-s, c]]` (the visual-CCW matrix in x-right/y-down) are both correct,
   and the composition `a_s * a_r * e^{i theta} * fs` is exactly the anchor form
   `(m/k) e^{i theta}`. The synthetic test must still lock this (see hand-over).
2. **Frame separation in `composite_placement` - passes.** The similarity (a, b) is fit
   on the four FULL-FRAME (doc size frame) corners; the reported panel corners are the
   CROP-box corners (size units, `_panel_crop`: map_box fractions * size, or (0,0,w,h)
   full frame) pushed through that same similarity. The composition of the three
   stage maps is an exact similarity in the w frame, so the full-frame fit is valid at
   the crop corners. `fit()`'s `size = row.size or [panel.width, panel.height]` matches
   `inkfit._size_frame`.
3. **Null phase - passes.** Both null `_match_theta` calls pass the UNROTATED panel
   (real or scrambled) plus the chosen theta; the rotation is applied inside, exactly
   as in the fit phase. Scramble recipe checked against 302b: same seed (20261012 =
   `inkfit.NULL_SEED`), same per-piece draw order (th, dx, dy), same R (`_rot2` form),
   clip, white background; the sheet shift matches 302b's DEM null
   (`ndi.shift(..., (-h/2, +w/2), order=0)`, cval 255 instead of NaN for an image).

**One real bug found and fixed (committed):** `panel_pieces` kept every autowalls keep
label, but the 302b reference `inkfit.template_pieces` drops labels that have zero of
`extract`'s 1-in-step sampled points (deterministic seed-0 subsample, step=2). A label
that 302b drops would still consume (th, dx, dy) draws from the single seeded RNG,
shifting every later piece's transform in the scrambled null image. Fix: select labels
through the sampled points, exactly as `template_pieces` does (`comp = lab[pts...]`;
a piece exists iff a sampled point hits its label). Verified on a synthetic panel:
identical (idx, length) piece lists, identical first scramble draw, valid scrambled
image; `ransac` recovers an exact planted similarity to 1e-14; `sheet_similarity`
returns |a| = 10, rot 0 deg for a known 10-merc-m/px sheet. Suite green: 68 passed,
1 skipped (the earlier known reds from other tasks are resolved on main; nothing mine
touches them). Matcher still live: /health -> zju-community/matchanything_eloftr on the
RTX 5060 Ti.

Next (session 4): write tests/test_surveyfit.py - the hermetic stub-server suite
(details in the task hand-over), then the real-service smoke, freeze, held-out
evaluator, one run.

### 2026-10-12 304 DECISION: hermetic stub-server test suite for the survey fit (tests/test_surveyfit.py written, not yet run); sign convention verified by code

   columns <= 198 and 2 rows >= 202 (the 302b half-box shift keeps 8 glyphs) ONLY when the
   grid centre is off-centre (pitch (198-c)/2 < p_x <= 198-c), while the plan frame (scale
   0.8, centre on site) needs the grid within ~155 px of the panel centre at every
   theta_d in {0,6,42}. Chosen: pitch 25/30 px, centre (195,235) - cols 120..270, rows
   220/250. Consequences (all measured): 8 shift survivors; all 14 glyphs in-frame at all
   three theta_d; min junk gap 35-93 px; and crucially the stub's rotation resolution is
   binary at the grid's 2 deg step (true theta: 14 hits; any 2-deg-off candidate: 4 hits),
   so the sent rotation always resolves to itself, never to a neighbour.

2. **Score ties, broken by a quality wobble, not a count cut.** With the binary hit gate,
   a call one fine step (2 deg) away from the true rotation still resolves and returns all
   14 true pairs (delta <= 3 band), so without further degradation it would TIE the true
   rotation's score and the sweep's first-max rule could land on 358/2 instead of 0. Fix
   (test-side only, no frozen-module change): the stub's returned plan-side points wobble
   by up to 0.6 px per degree of angular error, seeded per (theta, i) - deterministic and
   repeat-call-stable, mimicking a matcher whose match QUALITY degrades with rotation. The
   resulting score landscape is strictly ordered: delta 0 ~0.52 > delta 2 ~0.48 >> delta
   4-15 ~0.15-0.19 ~ junk-only ~0.15. The sweep is now deterministic: theta_d=0 -> 0, theta
   _d=6 -> 6, unique maxima in both cases (the fine-0 duplicate payload ties the coarse 0
   and the strict > keeps the first).

3. **Two crashes, both test-side.** (a) The anticipated zero-centroid ValueError in
   _resolve_theta (empty scrambled image): guarded. (b) NEW, unanticipated: scipy 1.18.1's
   ndi.center_of_mass(input, labels, index_array) returns a LIST OF (cy, cx) TUPLES (one
   per label), not a (cy-array, cx-array) pair - `cy, cx = ...` raises "too many values to
   unpack (expected 2)" whenever n != 2. _centroids rewritten to consume the list form. The
   single-mask form ndi.center_of_mass(mask) still returns a (cy, cx) tuple, so
   fit/surveyfit.py's panel_pieces (line 344) is unaffected - verified. (PITFALLS candidate.
   Note: the .venv the driver builds from requirements.txt pins this scipy; the code must
   match ITS behaviour, not an older one.)

  lexical environment, not globalThis); fix: bare `S` with a typeof guard. Both are now PITFALLS

## 2026-10-13 306d DECISION: iteration 166 - cassiobury judged WRONG (the 165 judge images had a 256x scale bug that masked the miss) and removed the 303 way; all five batch-2 lines written; the 3 remaining reds A/B-proven pre-existing

- The 165 judge images were misleading: j165e_compose.py computed metres-per-pixel as (360/2^z · 111194.93 · cos lat) - that is per TILE (256 px), not per pixel - so every marker (house 360 m NW, pond 453 m SE, the 4 anchors) was drawn 1-2 px from the site point and the whole fit LOOKED concentric. Fixed (mpp/256 = 0.74 at z17) and rebuilt: the drawn house (E -364..-47, N +179..+427) lands over the Cassiobury school complex (playfields + its rectangular pool), the drawn oval pond (E +406, N -202) mid-residential with NO water, and the plate's big wood masses east of the site, while the real park (woods, the round lake, the River Gade) lies WEST.
- The decisive fact (non-OSM fallback after overpass 504'd twice on both hosts): the Wikipedia infobox coordinate of Q5049456 Cassiobury House is 51.66500N 0.41889W = the catalog site point EXACTLY (kind garden) - and the article states the house was demolished 1927 and its site is now the housing between Temple Close and Parkside Drive (the red point sits in that housing). 165's hypothesis ("a 1933 replacement house on the old house's hill") is wrong: there is no 1933 house in Watford (the 1933 "Cassiobury" in Bedford, NY was built from THIS house's salvaged bricks; the surviving Grade II stables are Cassiobury Court). So the site point is the house site, and the fit puts the house ~360 m NW of it - on foreign (school) ground: the drawn works sit on the wrong side of the River Gade from the real ones. VERDICT: DELETE.

- SHELL/QUirks hit this session (for the record): (a) `python3 -c "...$d_fit.json"` in bash expands `$d_fit` as ONE variable name (underscore is a valid name char) - use `${d}_fit.json`; (b) PIL is only in the project .venv, not system python3; (c) `for ... in range(*range)` shadowing the builtin `range` raises `TypeError: range() argument after * must be an iterable`; (d) tuple-of-tuple lists do NOT flatten when unpacked (`L, y0, y1, x = cand[0]` where cand[0] = ((L,s,e), x) fails with "expected 4, got 2"); (e) scale bars on these plates are often SEGMENTED (black/white divisions) - the longest single dark run is one segment, you must merge all runs in the bar row band; the 2x-zoomed bar crop (read the image) is the most reliable measurement method.

## 2026-10-12 307 DECISION: split into 307a (place check), 307b (on-map placement), 307c (working space), 307d (owner check)
The owner's 307 rework has six acceptance boxes across two independent planes: the data side
(the queue must not pair a caption with the wrong site - a new place check in
tools/fit_queue.py) and the page side (the fit tool becomes a direct-placement tool - a new
web/fitkit.js extension). Split along the plane, in the order the owner needs them: a -> b
-> c -> d. No code this session; the split is the step.

Ground truth measured while planning (all verified by running code, iteration 107):
- The Devil's Dyke pair's root cause is data, not zoom: Allcroft fig. 217's title says
  "near Brighton"; its book-index evidence is a caption_coords tie on the name "Devil's
  Dyke" only (place: {}, score 1.0 vs runner-up 0.4), which the matcher accepted for the
  Cambridgeshire site. The catalog DOES contain the right site:
  devil-s-dyke-hillfort-q17674160 (Poynings, Mid Sussex, West Sussex; unbuilt). Ardoch
  (Allcroft n0354 "ARDOCH, PERTHSHIRE.", row place field "PERTHSHIRE") is the queue
  candidate for Coria and Vindomora (both Spain); the catalog (12,603 rows, name+aliases
  searched) has no Ardoch, so that mismatch goes to review, not a move.
- Recorded evidence conflicts are noisy for this job: 52 queue candidates carry one, but
  most are title words, not places ("Our", "Larned", "Allen", "Tourelles"; "France" ->
  the site Argentoratum is IN France, not a mismatch). The real ones look like "Alauna ->
  Ardoch Roman Fort" and "Bethlehem -> Bethlehem" (the catalog's Bethlehem Q2523914 is
  the DUTCH one, 6.61/53.38 - a genuine mismatch against the Palestine basilica plans).
  Hence the 307a rule: decide from KNOWN places only, fail open on unknown, and
  re-verify recorded verdicts offline (the evidence-check pattern).
- fit/propose.py already computes the anchor the page needs (bar scale / ratio at the
  book's ppi / site-size fallback; north arrow; 3-5 pairs). propose_for works for n0686
  (bar "0 100 200 300 400 Yards" + scale_bar box + 0-deg arrow: scale_m_px 0.3621, 5
  pairs centred on the site, coarse false). fit/propose.py and fit/review.py are
  stdlib-only (importable from tools/fit_queue.py); pipeline/books_match.py is NOT
  (it pulls pipeline/books.py -> PIL) - the check stays stdlib.
- The page already draws the ink on the map: index.html refit() maps P.inkUrl onto the
  'fit-prev' image source from the least-squares similarity of P.pairs (warpView() proves
  the image-source quad mechanism; a similarity's rotated rectangle is a parallelogram,
  so the affine the image source builds is exact). So "drawing starts on the map" = set
  P.pairs to the proposal's 5 pairs on open (least squares recovers the anchor exactly),
  then handlers edit the anchor and re-emit pairs; the saved doc stays pairs-shaped, so
  plan_fit.py/gate/one-site line are untouched.
- Baseline on this branch: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -> 73 passed, 1 skipped (green).

# Task 307a place-check

## 2026-10-12 307a DECISION: iteration 108 research, written late (iteration 109) - the place-check rule set and the page-work anchors
The iteration-108 session investigated the original 307a (the namesake place check) and
was re-tasked mid-session by the lead (box 1 -> 309 for agent c; agent a -> the page
work). It wrote the re-split record and the full 309 spec but never wrote the DECISIONS
entry its hand-over promised; this entry is that write-up, summarising with pointers
rather than restating (the detail lives in tasks/309-place-check.md, kept as reference,
and in the parent 307's Hand-over):
- Place-check rule set: decide from KNOWN places only - a mismatch only when a known
  caption place contradicts the site's (a different county within one country, a
different country, or resolved coordinates far outside the site's region); an unknown
place never mismatches (fail open - necessary because 52 queue candidates carry noisy
recorded conflicts that are mostly title words, not places); a place that contains the
site (a country-level word, the site's own county/name) is not a mismatch; re-verify
recorded verdicts offline (the evidence-check pattern: a recorded mismatch whose stored
coordinates no longer contradict is flagged, not silently kept).
- Measured cases: n0686 "The Devil's Dyke Camp, near Brighton" on the Cambridgeshire
dyke - the right site exists (devil-s-dyke-hillfort-q17674160, Poynings, West Sussex,
unbuilt) -> move there, not review; n0354 "ARDOCH, PERTHSHIRE." on the Spanish
Coria/Vindomora - the catalog (12,603 rows, name+aliases) has no Ardoch -> review with
the reason. Queue = 117 entries.
- Page-work anchors (307b): propose_for(n0686) -> scale_m_px 0.3621, 5 pairs centred on
the site, coarse false; refit() maps P.inkUrl onto the 'fit-prev' image source from the
least-squares similarity of P.pairs, so "the drawing starts on the map" = seed P.pairs
with the proposal's pairs, then handlers edit the anchor (drag/scale/rotate) and re-
emit pairs; the saved doc stays pairs-shaped, so plan_fit.py/the gate/the one-site line
are untouched.

- **fit/propose.py becomes root-aware** (added to 307ba's Touches): the four loaders

  (str(root), kind) so a temp tree never collides with the checkout's data; propose_for

  the cache is keyed by nothing today, so two roots in one process would silently read

Page-side design (307ba/307bb; full sketch in the 307b hand-over, the short version):

  (index.html:1707-1708 gains one script tag - the only index.html change; goal is the
  tag only). Wraps openPlan LAST in the chain and endFit (neither review.js nor
  fitqueue.js wraps endFit; fitqueue wraps renderList + saveFit, review wraps openPlan).
  _fk-prefixed saved names (the web/ PITFALL: one global lexical scope per page - a
  second script may not redeclare review.js's _renderList/_openPlan/...).

  the entry carries a propose (box 1's "the site's queued plan is the one picked");

  scrollZoom disabled while placed; P.pending nulled once moved > ~4 px - MapLibre's own

  save -> doc read back from the temp store (by:hand, pairs == final re-emitted set,

## 2026-10-12 307bb DECISION: the placement gestures live in fitkit.js by reassigning refit (no index.html footprint, no new map listeners) - designed in full, not yet coded
Investigation-only session: 307ba is done (suite 75+1, re-claimed at c5250a4 sync), so
307bb's start condition is met. No code written; the full implementation design (function
by function) is in 307bb's hand-over. Key decisions, all verified against the sources:

- **MapLibre 5.6.0 binds ALL gesture listeners on the canvas container, not the canvas**
  (web/vendor/maplibre-gl-5.6.0.js, readable UMD: mousedown/mousemove/mouseup/dblclick/
  click/wheel{passive:false} on getCanvasContainer(), mousemove{capture}/mouseup on
  document). Consequence: fitkit's gesture listeners go on the container; with
  dragPan/scrollZoom/touchZoomRotate/doubleClickZoom/boxZoom disabled while placed, the
  dispatcher (`if(!c.isEnabled())continue;`) skips them and none preventDefaults (the
  scrollZoom handler returns before its e.preventDefault() when disabled) - a
  later-registered container listener receives the events, so wheel/drag can own the mouse
  without fighting the map.
- **The 3px/4px disjointness is real, not assumed:** the always-enabled user-event handler
  records _mousedownPos on every mousedown and fires the map 'click' only when the
  mousedown->click distance is < clickTolerance (3 px, the page's default). Our move
  engages at >4 px, so a pinning click and a moving drag cannot both fire; we null
  P.pending the moment a move engages (a drag is not a pin).
- **Anchor refinement hooks through a wrapped refit, not a map listener:** the page's own
  map-click (pin), undo, clear and marker-dragend handlers all call the bare refit() - the
  global - so `refit = wrapper` sees every pair-count change: n grew -> push the pre-pin
  anchor(s) on P.anchorStack, refine the anchor by simFit over all pairs (view mode too:
  the anchor stays a similarity; verified algebraically simFit's a,b equal the re-emitted
  similarity's a,z0, so over the exact five it recovers the anchor to fp rounding),
  re-emit the five in place (mutate lon/lat, keep the objects - the marker dragend
  closures hold them), rebuild markers via the page's addPairMarker (push one at a time
  for 1..n labels); n shrank -> pop the stack (clear -> the anchor before the first pin;
  undo below the five-re-emit floor with an empty stack leaves the anchor untouched: the
  placement is inviolable). A drag gesture does NOT absorb the fit first (a move must not
  change mpx/rot); wheel/rotate do (so a previously dragged corner is absorbed into the
  anchor before the transform).
- **Gestures transform the anchor:** drag = centre += ground delta (unproject at both
  pointer points, exact at any zoom, fly-to-tolerant); wheel = mpx *= exp(-deltaY*0.0015)
  (the page canvas's own factor: wheel-up grows); shift+wheel = rot += deltaY*0.01 (1 deg
  per 100-unit notch). Applied rAF-coalesced (headless rAF works on this VM - the 307ba
  probe's fly-to animations ran). The page's fit pane already shows the fit's mpx/rot;
  fitkit additionally overwrites #fithint after each refit with the live anchor readout +
  gesture legend (box 1's "live scale and rotation in the panel").
- **Save needs no new code:** with P.pairs = re-emitted five (+ pins), the page's saveFit
  already writes exactly the doc the box asks for (same page-px frame: 307ba verified
  every current queue entry's served image IS its recorded size, so the row-size frame is
  the image frame). The fitqueue wrapper marks the site done; the one-site line runs as in
  part 2. The headless proof (box 3) pins all of it in pixels.
- **Deactivate placement at the TOP of the openPlan wrapper** (before the inner chain):
  review.js's wrapper pushes RV.pending pairs inside the chain and "Another plan" is
  endFit(false)->startFit->openPlan - a post-chain clear would let either inherit the
  previous placement; the 404-page path (part 3's served tree) still returns at the first
  P.img guard, byte-identical (keep that guard first).
